correctness.rationale: On exactly the listed 18 edges, simultaneous majority with unchanged ties defines a deterministic successor for each of the 2048 labelled states. The suffix starting at the first occurrence of the first repeated state is the entire least-period orbit; its start index is the least entry time. The independent fresh trajectory census reproduced 20 fixed states and 61 unordered two-cycles, the full orbit-level basin spectrum and all time-by-period counts. In particular the 48 depth-six starts all fix, and exhaustive checks gave F^8=F^6 but not F^7=F^5. The graph action commutes with the update because adjacency and current-bit ties are invariant under relabelling; filtering all degree-preserving vertex permutations by edge preservation exhausts automorphisms. The 12 surviving permutations give the reported period/class-size/basin-size signatures, with six spatial fixed classes and eleven two-cycle classes. Replay: python /workspace/branches/cef202a4-d94b-485b-a7fd-71a970bad7f4/fresh_majority_check.py; recorded fresh output fresh_majority_check.json in the same directory. This is exact finite enumeration, not a formal proof checker or a theorem on other graphs.

value.rationale: The Herschel graph is a canonical small non-Hamiltonian polyhedral graph with both odd- and even-degree update sites. A reproducible complete benchmark identifies which periods attract which starts, distinguishes maximum delay from orbit lengths, and detects that sharp delays occur only in fixed-point basins. Neither the universal period bound nor another graph's isolated counts supply this information.
